To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
lipid-stimulated intestinal apolipoproteins A-IV synthesis is dependent on vagal innervation and that this effect is mediated by distal gut receptors.

1) the vagus nerve is required for the ileal lipid-induced increase in jejunal apoA-I V synthesis, 2) the vagus does not mediate the ileal lipid-stimulated increase in apoA-I V gene expression, and 3) proximal gut lipid stimulates jejunal apoA I V production by both stimulating gene expression and enhancing translation.

1) vagotomy blocks lipid-stimulated synthesis of apoA-4 in the jejunum, 2) lipid-stimulated apoA-4 synthesis in the jejunm is independent of apoA-1 mRNA levels, and 3) direct perfusion of the jejunum stimulates apoA-1 synthesis and mRNA levels, and this effect is independent of vagus innervation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of intestinal apoliprotein A-IV production.
the role of intestinal apoliproteins in lipid absorption and metabolism.
the role of the intestine as an organ of lipid metabolism and transport.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the stimulation of jejunal synthesis by ileal lipid is mediated by the vagus nerve.
lipid-stimulated apoA-IV expression and synthesis is a complex phenomenon that is influenced by both local and neural factors.
vagotomy blocks lipid-induced stimulation of intestinal apolipooprotein A-IV synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vagal nerve is involved in the lipid-stimulated synthesis of apoA- IV, and the vagal nerve does not affect the mRNA level of apoA-4 in the small intestine.
the vagus nerve is required to transmit the signal from the distal gut that stimulates apoA-IV expression in the proximal gut.
the vagus is not required for the stimulation of intestinal lipid transport, but is required for lipid-stimulated jejunal apoA-Iv synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vagal innervation of the gut is important for lipid-mediated regulation of intestinal apoA- IV expression.
lipid-stimulated synthesis of apoA- IV is regulated by two distinct mechanisms.
the proximal gut is capable of responding to luminal lipid with an increase in apoAIV production, which is independent of vagus.
